pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
At Cranleigh C of E Primary, all children in Key Stage 2 learn French. We use the Language Angels scheme to make lessons engaging, enjoyable and carefully sequenced, so that knowledge builds year on year.
Why French?• Gives children the chance to communicate in another language.• Builds curiosity and awareness of other cultures.• Develops transferable skills such as listening, memory and problem-solving.• Prepares children for secondary school language learning and beyond.
How we teachWith Language Angels, children progress in:• Phonics – recognising and using French sounds.• Vocabulary – learning words and phrases around exciting topics.• Grammar – applying rules to speak and write with accuracy.• Speaking & Listening – songs, stories, role play and conversations.• Reading & Writing – from single words to sentences and short paragraphs by Year 6.
Lessons are interactive and accessible for all, with plenty of challenge for confident learners.
What children achieveBy the end of Year 6, pupils will:• hold a short conversation in French,• read and understand simple texts,• write using familiar vocabulary and grammar,• show confidence and enthusiasm about languages and cultures.
Progress is checked through regular tasks and assessments, ensuring children are ready for the next stage of learning.
For more information, please contact MFL Lead, Jill Mills, on 01483 273286.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Cranleigh C of E Primary School - To Nurture Belief and Ensure the Highest Standards of Learning for All
pageCache.text:
Music
We have a dedicated musical culture at Cranleigh C of E Primary. This has been created through our commitment to offer specialist instrumental lessons, experiential learning opportunities, participation in community events and ensuring our non-specialist teaching staff have a secure understanding of the curriculum they teach.
We use Charanga, a multi-award-winning music programme, to teach our Music lessons.
All curriculum documents can be found below.
We also offer weekly lessons to all Key Stage 2 children in drums, guitar and keyboard delivered by specialists from The Music Works; weekly instrumental lessons to all of Year 4 delivered by a specialist music teacher; the opportunity to join our school choir which practices each week and regularly performs at local community events and establishments; and visits to watch and listen to many different types of music at Cranleigh Arts Centre (recently, this has included a flute and harp performance, and jazz guitar). Alongside this Rocksteady attend the school weekly to deliver instrumental and vocal band lessons, supporting our children with their social and team skills through music engagement.
For more information, please contact the Music Lead, Emma Killick, on 01483 273286.

Art and Design
We use Cornerstones to provide an Art and Design curriculum that is well sequenced, coherent and builds pupils’ knowledge and skills over time. Our curriculum provides clear expectations as to what pupils will know and be able to do at given ‘end points’ throughout each year, and does so within the context of our specific school community.
The Art and Design projects develop pupils' skills and knowledge of visual elements, art forms, artists and art movements, and we provide specialist resources to support our pupils. Projects are placed alongside other subject projects where there are opportunities for making meaningful connections. Within each project, we provide opportunities for experiential learning and exhibiting, understanding the benefits of these to pupils' holistic development.
Our curriculum documents can be viewed below.
For more information, please contact the Art and Design Lead, Jo Conisbee, on 01483 273286.

pageCache.pageTitle: English - Cranleigh C of E Primary School - To Nurture Belief and Ensure the Highest Standards of Learning for All
pageCache.text:
English
We are passionate about ensuring that all children become confident and enthusiastic readers and writers, and we believe that phonics provides the foundations for these skills. In order to support this aim we follow the Little Wandle: Letters and Sounds Revised phonics scheme.
The Little Wandle progression information can be downloaded below.
In Reception, Year 1 and Year 2, we follow the Little Wandle Phonics and Fluency Scheme. Lexia is also used in Years 1 and 2 to support and assess reading.
In Year 3, children continue with Little Wandle Fluency. Those who have completed the phonics programme move on to reading independently, with progress tracked using Accelerated Reader. Children still on phonics are assessed through Little Wandle.
In Year 4, pupils still completing the phonics programme continue with Little Wandle, while others begin FREDs Fluent in Five. Assessment continues through Accelerated Reader and Little Wandle, depending on the child’s stage.
In Years 5 and 6, children follow FREDs Fluent in Five (Whole Class Reading), with progress monitored through Accelerated Reader. Any pupils still requiring phonics support are assessed using Little Wandle.
We also provide targeted interventions including Little Wandle Keep-Up, Little Wandle Rapid Catch-Up, Phonological Awareness, Learning Village, and Lexia to ensure every child gets the support they need.
Each class visits our school library weekly, Cranleigh Library each half-term, and reads a text together every half-term. This exposes pupils to a wide range of authors, settings, themes, and historical periods. These sessions are all designed to inspire a love of reading.
We follow the Talk for Writing approach to teach Writing throughout the school.
Talk for Writing has an outstanding impact on schools and is based on the principles of how people learn. Children move from imitating texts through to innovating them and then apply knowledge learnt in the final independent application stage.
Typically, schools have found that children initially double their rate of progress and, where the approach has been applied systematically across a setting, many schools have moved from dire results to outstanding success. Schools already performing well have not only increased attainment, but also enjoyment and engagement.
We use The Place Value of Punctuation and Grammar scheme from Grammarsaurus to support the teaching of Writing across the school. This carefully structured programme is designed to build children's knowledge and confidence in punctuation and grammar by linking each concept to its 'place value' within a sentence. Just as place value helps children understand the value of numbers, this approach helps them understand how different grammar and punctuation choices impact writing.
The scheme offers a consistent progression from Year 1 to Year 6, with engaging, well-sequenced lessons and visual supports. It enables pupils to apply grammatical concepts effectively in their own writing.
We use Letter-join throughout the school to teach handwriting. Documents attached below.
For more information, please contact our overall English Lead Natalie Jackson on 01483 273286.

Cranleigh Primary Friends Association (PTA)
The Cranleigh Primary Friends Association (The Friends) is our school’s Parent-Teacher Association (PTA) — a charitable group dedicated to supporting our school and fostering a vibrant community for children and parents alike.
They organise a variety of enriching activities and events, such as educational nature experiences, seasonal fayres, theatre outings, second-hand uniform sales, and community arts and social gatherings.
Entirely run by volunteers, they are always eager to welcome new members. To learn more and get involved, visit their Facebook group or telephone our school office on 01483 273286.

Safeguarding
Keeping our pupils safe at Cranleigh C of E Primary School is THE most important responsibility we have.
'Everyone who works with children has a responsibility for keeping them safe. No single practitioner can have a full picture of a child’s needs and circumstances and, if children and families are to receive the right help at the right time, everyone who comes into contact with them has a role to play in identifying concerns, sharing information and taking prompt action.' (Working Together to Safeguard Children: A guide to inter-agency working to safeguard and promote the welfare of children, p.11.)
We have signed up to The Church of England's Digital Charter as part of a pledge to make the online world a safer, kinder and fairer place for our community to be.
We have conducted a 360safe review of online safety, which is regularly updated, ensuring we are at least aligned with national standards. Additionally, we utilise robust filtering and monitoring systems, such as SENSO, deliver a comprehensive curriculum enriched by external contributors, including the NSPCC, to educate pupils on online safety, and use pupil voice to adapt our approach.
If you have any concerns regarding a child, please ask to speak to one of our safeguarding team below straight away:
Holly Falconer-Leeds: Head of Inclusion / Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL)
Tessa Church: Thrive Practitioner / Deputy Designated Safeguarding Lead (DDSL)
The Good Shepherd Trust contacts
Fiona Jenkins: Local Committee Safeguarding Link (fje.lc@cranleighprimary.co.uk)
Our school safeguarding team can be contacted on: DSL@cranleighprimary.co.uk
You can also contact one of the following:
C-Spa (Surrey Children's Services):
Phone: 0300 470 9100
Email: cspa@surreycc.gov.uk
NSPCC: 0808 800 5000
Police: 999 (where you believe a child is at immediate risk of harm)

Curriculum
Our rigorous, ambitious and relevant curriculum is designed to serve each child within our richly-diverse community, ensure the ‘highest standards of learning for all’ and prepare all children for a joyful life in the modern world.
Our commitment to the Christian faith and our six core values underpin our planned offer:
Our curriculum responds to, and embraces, an evolving community.
We are richly diverse and welcome families from various backgrounds.
The support we offer our families aims to build community by nurturing positive relationships and meaningful connections, overcoming any low literacy skills, and ensuring education is highly-valued by all. We consider ourselves compassionate and culturally responsive - ensuring we stay relevant to who and where our children, and their families, are.
We engage with our community; for example, through meetings with our local MP, Surrey Police, Directors at Surrey County Council, REMA, St. Nicolas Church and local councillors, as well stakeholder surveys, to ensure we serve our children in the best possible way.
We adapt our provision accordingly, ensure we provide our children with the demanding work they both deserve and seek, and ensure all children are given enrichment opportunities to enable them to learn about the world around them.
We pride ourselves on our commitment to sustain effective, and inclusive, communication, and hold exceptionally high expectations of ourselves, each other and our community. Our children are empowered to use their literacy, oracy, and digital communication skills, with scaffolding and support, to purposefully share and articulate their learning with others.
Our reflection procedures, which are research-focussed and include subject leadership time, responsive professional learning, both summative and formal assessments, and half-termly pupil progress meetings, enable us to refine our curriculum offer.
For general enquiries about our curriculum offer, please contact the office, at info@cranleighprimary.co.uk
